groups.title: In the water
groups.desc: The sea after the summer: still swimmable in October, cooling through November, and the coast's last big festival.

items.name: The sea, cooling by the week
items.teaser: Around 21°C on average in October, nearer 18°C in November: the last swims of the year, then wetsuit water
items.story: The Mediterranean off Barcelona holds its summer heat longer than the air. Climate averages put the October sea at about 21°C, with a range of roughly 18 to 24°C, after a peak of about 24°C in August; in 2025 the October average came in a little warmer. By November the average falls to about 18°C, with days between 16 and 20°C, cold enough that most swimmers reach for a wetsuit. The lows come in February, around 13°C. These are multi-year averages from climate sites, not a buoy reading, so the water on a given morning after a northerly blow can be colder.
items.why: Plan any guest swim or tender-and-swim stop for October; in November keep it short and have towels and warm drinks on board.
facts: Oct average about 21°C; Nov about 18°C (climate averages)
Averages hide cold snaps: check the morning reading before a swim

items.name: Sitges, down the coast: the film festival's last days
items.teaser: The 59th Sitges Film Festival runs 8–18 October: the last weekend is the coast's final big event of the season
items.story: Some 40 km south-west of Barcelona, Sitges turns over its seafront town each October to the Festival Internacional de Cinema Fantàstic de Catalunya, the fantasy and horror festival the town has hosted every October since 1968. The 59th edition runs from 8 to 18 October 2026, with new work from Nicolas Winding Refn, Hanna Bergholm and Léa Mysius announced in the line-up alongside restored cult titles. The 2025 edition ran 9–19 October, so the slot is fixed: the second and third weeks of October. Screenings fill the town's cinemas, and the closing weekend is the busiest.
items.why: Catch the closing weekend of 17–18 October, then lunch on the seafront before heading back up the coast.
facts: Sitges, about 40 km south-west of Barcelona
Ticketed screenings; prices on the festival site
Book the screening first; the closing-weekend sessions sell out

groups.title: In the sky
groups.desc: Shorter evenings and two meteor showers, neither of them a great show this year.

items.name: The clocks go back, Sunday 25 October
items.teaser: At 03:00 on Sunday 25 October the clocks return to 02:00: evenings in the port close an hour earlier
items.story: Spain leaves summer time in the early hours of Sunday 25 October 2026: on the mainland and in the Balearics, at 03:00 the clocks go back to 02:00, and that Sunday has 25 hours. The date comes from the calendar set by the BOE order PCM/186/2022, and it is the last change that order lists; no rule yet ends the twice-yearly change in Spain. The same Sunday is the second day of 48h Open House BCN, so anyone with a morning visit booked gains an hour. From then on sunset comes an hour earlier by the clock.
items.why: After 25 October book sunset drinks and terrace tables an hour earlier than a summer habit would suggest.
facts: Mainland Spain and the Balearics (Canaries an hour earlier)
Phones change by themselves; ship's clocks, crew rotas and bookings made in summer do not

items.name: Two meteor showers, both under a bright Moon
items.teaser: Orionids peak before dawn on 22 October and the Leonids around 17 November, both with the Moon in the way
items.story: Two annual meteor showers fall in this window, and neither will be generous in 2026. The Orionids, debris from Halley's Comet, peak on the night of 21–22 October with the best rates before dawn on the 22nd, but a waxing gibbous Moon about three-quarters lit will wash out all but the brightest. The Leonids peak on the night of 16–17 November by the American Meteor Society's count (17–18 by the Almanac), with the Moon about 45 per cent lit and expected to set before dawn, leaving a dark window. Even then the expected rate is 10 to 15 an hour under dark skies, and no storm is forecast.
items.why: From a lit marina, skip both; at anchor well offshore in the pre-dawn of 17 November, look east and up.
facts: Orionids peak 21–22 Oct; Leonids 16–17 or 17–18 Nov 2026
Dark sky away from the city lights; at sea is best
The Leonids' dark window is after moonset, before dawn

groups.title: On the plate
groups.desc: Chestnuts and panellets for Tots Sants, a late mushroom season, and a new MICHELIN guide.

items.name: The Castanyada: chestnuts, panellets, moniatos
items.teaser: On the eve of All Saints, Catalans eat roast chestnuts, sweet potatoes and pine-nut panellets with sweet wine
items.story: The Castanyada began as a family meal for the dead: the Gran Enciclopèdia Catalana describes chestnuts and panellets eaten after supper with sweet wine and a rosary said for the departed, a meal later moved to the eve of 1 November. Today it is a social dinner, with roasted chestnuts, baked moniatos (sweet potatoes) and panellets, small balls of marzipan rolled in pine nuts or finished with almond, coconut, chocolate or coffee, served with moscatell, rancio or cava. Tots Sants falls on Sunday 1 November in 2026, and the pastry shops fill their windows with panellets through the last week of October.
items.why: Buy a box of pine-nut panellets for the crew mess in the last days of October; they are gone from the windows within a week.
facts: Eve of Tots Sants, Sat 31 Oct; Tots Sants Sun 1 Nov 2026
Pastry shops and chestnut stalls across the city
Panellets are sold by weight; ask the price per box
Pine-nut panellets are the classic; pair them with a glass of moscatell

items.name: Mushrooms: a late, thin season so far
items.teaser: Drought has delayed the 2026 rovellons and ceps: late-September rain may bring them by the end of October
items.story: Autumn in Catalonia usually means rovellons, ceps and trompetes on the market stalls and in the rice. In 2026 the season is late. On 2 October Ara reported mycologists and pickers finding very little, with the woods dry after drought and high temperatures, and the hope that the rains at the end of September would show results in two or three weeks. 3Cat reported mushrooms in parts of the Pyrenees, but not widely and not in quantity, and the Cal Rosal mushroom market opened with small amounts of fresh specimens; it runs to early November. Expect high prices and short supply until the rains pay off.
items.why: Ask the market stall where its rovellons were picked: local wild ones are scarce this year, so imports fill the gap.
facts: Season delayed in Oct 2026; usually Sept to Nov
Market stalls; the Boqueria is the city's best-known
High this year; ask the price per kilo
If the menu says 'rovellons' this month, ask whether they are local

items.name: The MICHELIN Guide Spain 2027, Tuesday 24 November
items.teaser: The 2027 stars are revealed on 24 November in Huesca: for the first time the gala goes to Aragón
items.story: MICHELIN will reveal its Spain 2027 selection on 24 November 2026 at the Palacio de Congresos de Huesca, in the Auditorio Carlos Saura, the first time the gala has been held in Aragón; Málaga hosted the 2026 edition and Murcia the one before. Carmelo Bosque of the one-star Lillas Pastia coordinates the gala dinner. For Barcelona, the night decides whether the city's star tables hold or move: Mont Bar went from one star to two at the 2026 gala in November 2025. Bookings at any promoted table tighten within days of the announcement.
items.why: If a table on the guest list is likely to gain a star, book it before 24 November, not after.
facts: Palacio de Congresos de Huesca (Aragón), not Barcelona
Invitation only; the results go online the same evening
Book promoted Barcelona tables the week before

groups.title: In the calendar
groups.desc: Architecture weekend, the jazz festival in full swing, and Verdi at the Liceu.

items.name: 48h Open House BCN, 24–25 October
items.teaser: One weekend when private buildings, offices and new houses open their doors to the public across the city
items.story: 48h Open House BCN is Barcelona's yearly architecture festival: for one weekend, buildings that are normally closed, from modernista apartments to new housing, offices and research centres, open to the public with guided or self-guided visits. The 2025 edition ran on 25–26 October; Open House Worldwide lists the 2026 festival for Saturday 24 and Sunday 25 October. Some buildings run on queues, others on pre-booked slots that go within hours of release. The Sunday is also the day the clocks go back.
items.why: Pick two or three buildings in one district and walk between them; the queues for the famous names eat the day.
facts: Sat 24–Sun 25 Oct 2026 (check the festival site; one listing still says 'to be confirmed')
Pre-booked slots go quickly; queue-only buildings are best early morning

items.name: The Barcelona Jazz Festival, 58th edition
items.teaser: 77 concerts in eleven venues until the end of December: Samara Joy debuts at the Palau on 13 November
items.story: The Voll-Damm Festival Internacional de Jazz de Barcelona opened its 58th edition on 29 September with Zucchero at the Palau de la Música Catalana, the first of three years leading up to its 60th anniversary. The programme runs to the end of December with 77 concerts in eleven venues and more than 600 musicians, from the Palau to Jamboree, La Paloma, Sala Apolo and the Conservatori del Liceu. Samara Joy makes her Palau debut on 13 November, two days after her 27th birthday; Dianne Reeves, Branford Marsalis, Ibrahim Maalouf and Vicente Amigo are also on the bill.
items.why: For one night, choose the Palau de la Música: the modernista hall is half the reason to go.
facts: 29 Sep–end Dec 2026; Samara Joy Fri 13 Nov
Palau de la Música Catalana and ten other venues
Per concert; prices on the festival site
Book the Palau nights first: they sell out before the club dates

items.name: Verdi's Requiem at the Liceu, 3–4 November
items.teaser: Lise Davidsen sings Verdi's Requiem in concert at the Gran Teatre del Liceu, the week after Tots Sants
items.story: The Liceu opened its 2026–27 season on 25 September with a new Aida directed by Shirin Neshat, which closes on 15 October. Its next big night is a concert, not a staging: Verdi's Requiem on 3 and 4 November, with the Norwegian soprano Lise Davidsen. Written for the dead, it falls in the week after All Saints. The season has 194 performances in total, with nine staged operas, among them a new Magic Flute and Jenůfa, and four concert operas.
items.why: The red-and-gold horseshoe of the rebuilt 1847 house is worth seeing from the upper tiers: book there.
facts: Gran Teatre del Liceu, La Rambla
Check the start time on the ticket: concert nights can differ from opera nights

groups.title: Spring: the book, the rose and the sound
groups.desc: Sant Jordi in April, then two festivals that fill June.

items.name: Sant Jordi, 23 April
items.teaser: Catalonia's day of the book and the rose: the whole city becomes a bookstall
items.story: On 23 April, the feast of Sant Jordi, Catalonia's patron saint, the custom is to give a rose and a book. The Rambla, Passeig de Gràcia and every square fill with bookstalls and rose sellers, authors sign at trestle tables, and it is a working day, so the crowd comes at lunch and after work. In 2027 it falls on a Friday.
items.why: Walk Passeig de Gràcia at midday and buy one book and one rose: that is the whole ritual.
facts: La Rambla, Passeig de Gràcia and squares citywide
Free to walk; books and roses for sale
It is a working day: the stalls are busiest at lunch and after 18:00

items.name: Primavera Sound, 2–6 June 2027
items.teaser: The big indie and pop festival at the Parc del Fòrum, with its 2027 line-up already out
items.story: Primavera Sound takes over the Parc del Fòrum, the concrete esplanade at the end of the Diagonal by the sea, for its early-June edition. The 2027 dates are 2–6 June, with the main programme on 3–5 June and opening and closing events around it; the line-up was announced in October 2026 and tickets went on sale on 8–9 October. Expect the Fòrum's stages to run from late afternoon until well after dawn.
items.why: Book hotels and berths early: the city is full for the festival weekend.
facts: The Fòrum is by the sea: a tender drop-off beats the metro crush

items.name: Sónar, mid-June
items.teaser: Barcelona's festival of advanced music and new media art: by day at Fira Montjuïc, by night at Fira Gran Via
items.story: Sónar, the electronic music and digital arts festival founded in 1994, runs over three days in mid-June, with daytime programmes and late-night stages. In 2026 it ran from 18 to 20 June. A listing site gives 17–19 June 2027, but the festival had not published its 2027 line-up or venues when we checked, so treat those dates as a placeholder until the official announcement.
items.why: Wait for sonar.es before booking around it.
facts: Fira Montjuïc (day) and Fira Gran Via (night) in past editions
Day and night are separate tickets

groups.title: Summer: fire and the festes
groups.desc: Sant Joan's bonfires, a month of theatre at Montjuïc and Gràcia's decorated streets.

items.name: Sant Joan, the night of 23 June
items.teaser: The shortest night: bonfires, fireworks, coca de Sant Joan and cava on the beaches
items.story: The revetlla de Sant Joan, on the night of 23 June, is Catalonia's midsummer: fireworks from dusk until long after midnight, bonfires, the flame brought from Canigó, and the coca de Sant Joan, a flat sweet bread topped with candied fruit and pine nuts, eaten with cava. The beaches fill until dawn, and 24 June is a holiday. In 2027 the night falls on a Wednesday.
items.why: Watch from the water if you can: the beaches are packed and fireworks go off at street level all night.
facts: Night of 23 Jun every year (Wed 23 Jun 2027)
Buy the coca from a pastry shop that afternoon; they sell out

items.name: Grec Festival, July
items.teaser: Barcelona's summer festival of theatre, dance and music, centred on the open-air Teatre Grec on Montjuïc
items.story: The Grec began in 1976 and marked its 50th anniversary in 2026, running from 29 June to 31 July across some fifty spaces in the city. Its heart is the Teatre Grec, an open-air amphitheatre cut into a former quarry on Montjuïc in 1929, where the big productions play under the summer sky. 2027 dates are not yet published; it usually runs from the end of June through July.
items.why: Book a night at the Teatre Grec itself and arrive early to sit in the garden.
facts: Teatre Grec, Passeig de Santa Madrona 36, Montjuïc, and venues citywide
Bring a layer: Montjuïc evenings cool after dark

items.name: Festes de Gràcia, mid-August
items.teaser: A week when Gràcia's streets compete with hand-made decorations, with concerts every night
items.story: Each August the Gràcia district holds its festa major, and its streets and squares dress themselves in decorations that residents build over months, competing in the Concurs de Carrers Guarnits. In 2026 the festival ran 15–21 August, opened on 14 August, with 23 decorated streets and squares and more than 900 activities. It usually starts on 15 August, the feast of the Assumption, and the streets are judged early in the week.
items.why: Go in the morning to see the decorations without the night crowd.
facts: Usually 15 Aug for a week (2026: 15–21 Aug)
The decorations are best seen by day; the concerts run late

groups.title: Autumn and winter: the city's own
groups.desc: The national day, the patron's festival and the Christmas fair with its canelons.

items.name: La Diada, 11 September
items.teaser: Catalonia's national day: flags on the balconies, wreaths, and marches through the centre
items.story: The Diada Nacional de Catalunya on 11 September marks the fall of Barcelona in 1714 at the end of the siege in the War of the Spanish Succession. The day is a holiday, with flowers laid at the monument to Rafael Casanova, senyeres on the balconies and, in many years, large marches along the main avenues. Shops and many restaurants close for the day. In 2027 it falls on a Saturday.
items.why: Expect road closures in the centre: plan transfers around the march.
facts: Many shops close; book lunch ahead

items.name: La Mercè, around 24 September
items.teaser: Barcelona's own festival: giants, human towers, correfoc and free concerts
items.story: The city's festa major honours the Mare de Déu de la Mercè, patron of Barcelona, whose day, 24 September, is a local holiday. In 2026 the festival ran Wednesday 23 to Sunday 27 September, with Shanghai as guest city and events spread for the first time across all ten districts. Expect the gegants, castells in Plaça Sant Jaume, the correfoc and free concerts. In 2027 the 24th falls on a Friday.
items.why: See the castells in Plaça Sant Jaume on the morning of the 24th.
facts: Around 24 Sep (2026: 23–27 Sep; 24 Sep 2027 is a Friday)
Citywide; Plaça Sant Jaume for the castells
For the correfoc, cover arms and head with cotton

sources.label: idealista: Festes de la Mercè 2026 dates and programme

items.name: Fira de Santa Llúcia and Sant Esteve canelons
items.teaser: The Christmas fair in front of the Cathedral, then canelons on 26 December
items.story: The Fira de Santa Llúcia, the Christmas market on the Pla de la Seu and Avinguda de la Catedral, dates back to 1786 and sells nativity figures, moss, holly, caganers and the Tió de Nadal log. Listings for 2026 give a start between 26 and 28 November and an end on 23 December; the city had not confirmed the dates when we checked. On Sant Esteve, 26 December, a holiday in Catalonia, families eat canelons made from the Christmas meat.
items.why: Buy a caganer at the fair; eat the canelons at a traditional house after Christmas.
facts: Fair late Nov–about 23 Dec 2026 (unconfirmed); Sant Esteve Sat 26 Dec 2026
Pla de la Seu, in front of the Cathedral

venue_hot.v12-la-cova-fumada: Closed Sundays, so not on 25 Oct or Tots Sants (1 Nov 2026); go Mon–Fri 09:00–15:30 or Saturday to 14:30 for the bomba (checked 15 Oct 2026).
